title: Operations Research I (Optimization)
description: Operations Research I (Optimization) develops deterministic OR modeling and methods: linear and integer programming, duality and sensitivity, networks, branch-and-bound, nonlinear and dynamic programming basics, solvers, and applied modeling practice.

topics.title: Linear Programming Formulation
topics.description: Linear programming is the modeling language of deterministic operations research. Students learn to translate decisions, limits, and goals into objective functions and constraints.

children.title: Decision Variables
children.description: Students learn to define the controllable choices in a problem clearly enough that a solver or analyst can act on them.

children.title: Objective Functions
children.description: The objective expresses what the model is trying to maximize or minimize.

children.title: Constraints
children.description: Constraints encode resource limits, requirements, balances, capacities, and policy rules.

children.title: Model Assumptions
children.description: Students learn that linear models are powerful but only credible when assumptions are visible.

topics.title: The Simplex Method
topics.description: The simplex method is the classic algorithmic engine for linear programming. It teaches students what solvers are doing geometrically and algebraically.

children.title: Geometry of Linear Programs
children.description: Students learn why optima occur at extreme points of feasible regions.

children.title: Standard Form
children.description: Standard form prepares models for algorithmic solution.

children.title: Simplex Tableau Mechanics
children.description: Tableau calculations show how the algorithm moves from one basic feasible solution to a better one.

children.title: Special Cases
children.description: Students learn how to recognize model or solution conditions that affect interpretation.

topics.title: Duality and Sensitivity Analysis
topics.description: Duality reveals the economic meaning of constraints, while sensitivity analysis explains how solutions change when data changes.

children.title: Primal-Dual Relationships
children.description: Students learn that every LP has a related dual problem with complementary economic meaning.

children.title: Shadow Prices
children.description: Shadow prices quantify the marginal value of constrained resources.

children.title: Complementary Slackness
children.description: Complementary slackness links primal and dual optimal solutions.

children.title: Sensitivity Ranges
children.description: Sensitivity analysis supports decisions when coefficients are estimates rather than fixed truths.

topics.title: Transportation and Assignment Problems
topics.description: Transportation and assignment models are structured LPs that appear in logistics, staffing, routing, allocation, and matching problems.

children.title: Transportation Model Structure
children.description: Students learn how supply, demand, and shipping costs create a network-like LP.

children.title: Transportation Algorithms
children.description: Specialized methods exploit model structure for efficient solution.

children.title: Assignment Model Structure
children.description: Assignment problems allocate agents to tasks one-to-one.

children.title: Applications and Variants
children.description: Students learn how these models appear in practical operations settings.

topics.title: Network Optimization
topics.description: Network optimization uses nodes and arcs to model flow, routes, capacity, and connectivity in systems like logistics, communications, and infrastructure.

children.title: Network Modeling Basics
children.description: Students learn to represent systems as graph structures with flows and costs.

children.title: Shortest Path Problems
children.description: Shortest path models support routing, scheduling, and least-cost path decisions.

children.title: Maximum Flow and Minimum Cut
children.description: Max-flow models identify throughput limits in capacitated networks.

children.title: Minimum-Cost Flow
children.description: Minimum-cost flow unifies transportation, transshipment, and capacity-constrained routing.

topics.title: Integer Programming
topics.description: Integer programming handles yes/no, count, sequencing, and logical decisions that cannot be modeled honestly with continuous variables alone.

children.title: Integer and Binary Variables
children.description: Students learn when integrality is necessary for real decisions.

children.title: Logical Modeling
children.description: Integer programming can encode if-then relationships and fixed-charge decisions.

children.title: Modeling Common Applications
children.description: Students connect IP to facility location, scheduling, capital budgeting, and blending decisions.

children.title: LP Relaxation
children.description: Relaxations help students understand bounds, difficulty, and algorithm behavior.

topics.title: Branch-and-Bound Method
topics.description: Branch-and-bound is the core exact solution framework for integer programming. It shows how solvers search intelligently without enumerating every possibility.

children.title: Branching
children.description: Branching splits a difficult integer problem into smaller subproblems.

children.title: Bounding
children.description: Bounds tell the algorithm which subproblems are promising and which can be ignored.

children.title: Fathoming Rules
children.description: Students learn why a node can be safely discarded.

children.title: Solver Behavior
children.description: Branch-and-bound builds intuition for why some MIPs are easy and others are hard.

topics.title: Nonlinear Programming Basics
topics.description: Nonlinear programming introduces models where objectives or constraints are curved. Students learn basic ideas without losing the OR I focus on modeling and decision support.

children.title: Sources of Nonlinearity
children.description: Students learn why real systems often violate linear assumptions.

children.title: Unconstrained Optimization
children.description: Unconstrained problems introduce gradients and curvature.

children.title: Constrained Nonlinear Problems
children.description: Constraints introduce feasible-direction and multiplier ideas.

children.title: Local Versus Global Optima
children.description: Students learn why nonlinear problems can be harder to interpret than LPs.

topics.title: Dynamic Programming
topics.description: Dynamic programming solves multistage decisions by breaking them into states, decisions, transitions, and value functions.

children.title: Principle of Optimality
children.description: Students learn why an optimal policy must contain optimal subdecisions.

children.title: Deterministic Dynamic Programming
children.description: Deterministic models show the core recursion before uncertainty is added.

children.title: Value Functions
children.description: Value functions summarize future consequences of current states.

children.title: Curse of Dimensionality
children.description: Students learn why DP is powerful but can become computationally expensive.

topics.title: Optimization Software
topics.description: Optimization software turns models into usable decisions. Students learn solver workflows, model debugging, and responsible interpretation of computational results.

children.title: Solver Landscape
children.description: Students learn the difference between modeling languages, solvers, and solver services.

children.title: Modeling Workflow
children.description: A repeatable workflow helps students build, solve, and audit optimization models.

children.title: Debugging Models
children.description: Optimization models fail in predictable ways, and students need a troubleshooting process.

children.title: Communicating Results
children.description: Optimization output must be translated into decisions, assumptions, and limitations.

topics.title: Convexity and Optimality Conditions
topics.description: This added synthesis topic gives students the conceptual bridge from LP/IP methods to modern convex and nonlinear optimization.

children.title: Convex Sets and Functions
children.description: Convexity explains when local optima are globally meaningful.

children.title: Gradient and Newton Ideas
children.description: Gradient-based methods show how nonlinear solvers use local derivative information.

children.title: KKT Conditions
children.description: KKT conditions generalize optimality for constrained nonlinear problems.

children.title: Interior-Point Preview
children.description: Interior-point methods connect modern LP and convex optimization algorithms.

topics.title: Modeling Practice, Solver Workflow, and Applications
topics.description: This added capstone topic emphasizes the practical skill of building credible decision models and using optimization results in real operations settings.

children.title: Model-Building Discipline
children.description: Students learn to move from a messy decision problem to a transparent mathematical model.

children.title: Applications Portfolio
children.description: Students see recurring OR model patterns across industries.

children.title: Scenario and Sensitivity Workflow
children.description: Good optimization practice tests whether recommendations survive plausible data changes.

children.title: Ethics and Implementation
children.description: Optimization affects people, resources, and organizations, so implementation must consider fairness, usability, and accountability.
